thread:
tess: Quick FYI — I'm flipping the small-batch fastpath to canary (10% traffic) for the embeddings ingress tonight. It prioritizes requests with <=8 vectors and payload <=50KB. Doing this to cut p95 for interactive embed lookups.

nate: nice. can you paste the exact rules/thresholds? want to make sure the console cost panels and quotas map correctly. :eyes:

maya: are we treating fastpath requests as separate billing units? need to know for the cost dashboard and tenant chargebacks.

alex: config in the canary: ```json
{
  "fastpath": true,
  "max_vectors": 8,
  "max_bytes": 51200,
  "priority_weight": 0.65,
  "max_concurrency_per_tenant": 50
}
```

maya: thanks. if priority_weight is <1 then runtime will schedule smaller batches earlier; but that can starve large batch throughput during spikes. we should have a fallback circuit.

sam: agree — add a degradation rule: if global backlog > 2000 requests OR large-batch throughput drops >20% we disable fastpath for that AZ.

nate: console implications: want a toggle in the routing config UI (per-region, per-tenant) + a telemetry tag on requests so dashboards can filter. proposal: add label `routing.fastpath=small` to traces/metrics.

tess: yep adding `routing.fastpath=small` to trace/span attrs and adding a metric vector `embed.fastpath_requests_total{tenant=...,region=...,enabled=true}`. also will emit `embed.fastpath_fallbacks_total` when we circuit-break.

maya: for quotas — how do we count units? currently billing counts tokens/embedding-units at ingestion. small fastpath shouldn't change billing math but we do need a console note: "fastpath is performance optimization, billing unchanged". ops & sales asked to have that copy.

alex: telemetry ask: new dashboard panels: p50/p95/p99 for fastpath vs normal, consumption delta (tokens/sec), and large-batch backlog gauge. also add a heatmap of tenant-level fastpath adoption.

sam: rollout plan: 10% global for 48h -> check p95 improvement and large-batch SLA impact -> 20% -> per-tenant opt-in for a small set of customers -> full. Rollback criteria: p95 regresses by >10% for large-batch pipelines OR embed.fastpath_fallbacks_total spikes > 5x baseline.

nate: can we add a console alert rule: fastpath_fallback_rate > 0.5% for 5m => page eng-runtime? and a non-urgent signal for customer-facing metric drift.

tess: yep will add both. infra-bot: starting canary at 2024-08-12T03:00Z on 10% traffic.

infra-bot: deploy started: canary-fastpath-v2 to embed-ingress (canary=10%). link: https://deploys.internal/redwood/deploy/fastpath-v2 :rocket:

maya: one more: please ensure preflight returns a header `x-routing-path: fastpath` so client SDKs can surface explanatory UX (fast vs batched).

alex: i'll wire that into the console API docs and example SDK snippet.

sam: assigning actions: tess -> telemetry + alerts, alex -> console toggle + docs, nate -> dashboard panels, maya -> draft customer copy regarding billing + FAQ. check back after 48h. :thumbsup:

tess: thanks team — will post canary metrics in #eng-platform after 1h and update the runbook with rollback commands.
